name: Bluff
description: Bluff (also known as 'I Doubt It' or IDI) is a tactical shedding game based on deception and rank counting. Players take turns playing cards face-down, claiming they all match the current required rank. Anyone can challenge a claim; if the liar is caught, they take the entire central pile, but if the challenger is wrong, they take it instead. It is a universal social game that rewards a 'poker face' and sharp memory.

history.origins: Bluff is a regional variant of the children's game I Doubt It, played in West Bengal, India, where players may lay several cards while claiming they all match the required rank. It belongs to the broader family of 'Cheat' games based on deception and card counting.
timeline: 1800s: Variations like 'Cheat' and 'Bullshit' emerge in European folk culture.
1900s: Standardized as 'I Doubt It' in American family game books.
Present: A perennial party game favorite worldwide, frequently adapted for digital platforms.
history.cultural: Universal appeal across cultures; known as 'Mogeln' in Germany and 'Verish' ne Verish'' in Russia.
history.evolution: The game shifted from simple children's play into a more sophisticated psychological duel as competitive card-counting strategies were developed by adult players.

setup.dealing: Deal the entire deck as evenly as possible clockwise. Players keep their hands private but their card count visible.

rules.objective: Be the first player to empty your hand of all cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Establish Rank**: A target rank (e.g., Queens) is chosen for the round. 2. **Turn**: Each player in turn must play 1 to 4 cards face-down, claiming they are the target rank. 3. **Challenge**: Any player can shout 'Bluff!' or 'I Doubt It!' after a play. 4. **Reveal**: If challenged, the played cards are revealed. 5. **Penalty**: If the player lied, they take the entire table pile. If they were truthful, the challenger takes the pile. 6. **Rank Change**: The rank changes to the next in sequence (A-2-3...) after a successful challenge or when a new round starts.
keyRules: You must play at least one card every turn.
Any player can challenge any other player's claim.
Successful challenges reset the central pile.

strategy.basic: Only bluff when you have no choice or when you hold very few cards of the current rank. Use your real cards first to thin your hand.
strategy.intermediate: Rank Tracking: Count how many cards of the current rank have been played. If you hold three Kings and someone else plays two, you know they are lying.
strategy.advanced: The Desperation Bluff: If you are down to your last card and it doesn't match the rank, you MUST bluff. Try to play it quickly and confidently to deter challenges.
tips: Watch for 'Hesitation Tells'—players often pause longer when they are about to lie.
If you win a challenge and set the next rank, choose one where you hold several cards.

variations.name: Bullshit (Sequential)
variations.description: Rank increments every turn (Aces, then 2s, then 3s...) rather than staying the same for a round.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes the sequence of ranks between rounds; the core engine loop and actions stay the same.

scoring.description: No points are awarded; the objective is purely hand-emptying.
scoring.winCondition: Successful shedding of all hand cards.

synthesis.shortDescription: The timeless bluffing game. Play cards face-down and claim they're something. Anyone can call your bluff—but they'd better be right. The liar and the wrongful accuser both pay. Sharpen your poker face and master the cards.
